46.limitations: OPEN, city journey (bug bash 2026-08-10): the two blocking dialogs render before the app shell that injects the global box-sizing reset, so their card is 19px wider than every phone viewport (339px at 320, 394 at 375, 409 at 390) and the corners clip; desktop is unaffected but the card is 565px rather than the intended 480px. Three P3s also remain: the city-search combobox ignores ArrowUp/ArrowDown and never sets aria-activedescendant (its suggestions are real buttons inside the focus trap, so the dialog stays keyboard-completable); the Hindi UI shows English city names because the gazetteer is English-only; and the document title stays English behind a Hindi first-run dialog. NOT YET BUILT: signed-in cross-device account sync (city-preference contract rule 4 and its sign-in conflict rule) — the local/device and shared-link behaviour is live, but a city still does not follow the user to another browser or device, and no UI claims otherwise. Related copy debt: the footer line 'computed on your device · no account' is accurate today and becomes false the day Jyotish accounts ship. NOT VERIFIABLE BY AGENT: real physical keyboard traversal and screen-reader voicing of both blocking dialogs — the harness delivers no key events to the page (proven with a capture listener), so trap behaviour was verified by dispatching at the live handler, not by native tabbing; and the geolocation success path, since the test browser had location permission denied at profile level, so the device-location distance cap is proven by an executing gate rather than a live GPS grant. Earlier parked items still stand: sixteen native <option> nodes will not scale inside the browser dropdown popup, and the Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon was switched OFF by owner decision on 2026-08-02.
46.shortTermImpact: The blocking city question no longer fires when the link and the remembered city are the same place, which previously stopped every device-location user who opened a Ganak link for their own city and offered them two identically-worded buttons. 'Use my device location' no longer names a city hundreds of kilometres away in the wrong timezone, so it can no longer state confidently wrong sunrise, tithi and muhurat times. A deliberate Hindi choice is now remembered, so a Hindi-first reader no longer re-picks Hindi on every visit. The remaining phone-width clipping is cosmetic; nothing is unreadable and no content is lost.
46.longTermImpact: Places are now compared by timezone and real distance rather than exact coordinate text, so the gazetteer, the online geocoder and device GPS can disagree on precision or label without producing a false conflict — a class of bug that would otherwise have recurred with every new place source. The device-location distance cap converts a silent wrong-timezone answer into visible bilingual guidance, keeping panchang correctness ahead of convenience. Both rules are pinned by gates that execute the shipped functions, so a future refactor cannot reintroduce either defect green.
